title: New-Hire Onboarding
description: The most important things to know in your first week — how Quiz Lab ships, how work flows, and how to add a pack.

questions.prompt: Where do quiz pack JSON files live in the repo?
questions.explanation: Each pack is a single JSON file in app/src/lib/data/packs/, named for its id (Architecture Overview; Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: Which framework is Quiz Lab built with?
questions.explanation: Quiz Lab is a SvelteKit 2 app built with Vite and the static adapter (@sveltejs/adapter-static) (Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: At which route does a pack with id "onboarding" play?
questions.explanation: Each pack renders at the route /play/{packId}, so this pack plays at /play/onboarding (Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: What actually deploys Quiz Lab to production?
choices: Pushing the build to a Vercel project
Merging a PR to main, which triggers a GitHub Actions build that publishes to GitHub Pages
A nightly cron job that rebuilds the site
questions.explanation: The entire pipeline is: merge to main → GitHub Actions build → GitHub Pages. There is no separate deploy step (Architecture Overview; Engineering Handbook).

questions.prompt: Which statement about Quiz Lab's backend is correct?
choices: It uses a Postgres database for leaderboards
It has no server runtime and no database — it's a fully prerendered static site
It runs a Node API server
Content is stored in a headless CMS
questions.explanation: Quiz Lab is fully prerendered with no server runtime and no database; all content ships in the build (Architecture Overview).

questions.prompt: How many answer choices must each question have?
questions.explanation: The Pack Authoring Guide requires the choices array to have exactly 4 options.

questions.prompt: What does a question's correctIndex field hold?
choices: The text of the correct answer
A zero-based index (0–3) pointing into the choices array
The difficulty level of the question
The id of the correct choice
questions.explanation: correctIndex is an integer 0–3 that indexes into choices — the answer is stored as a position, not as text (Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: What is the valid range for a question's difficulty field?
questions.explanation: difficulty is the integer 1, 2, or 3, rendered as ★ to ★★★ (Pack Authoring Guide; Product Vision & Glossary).

questions.prompt: In Studio AI, what is an "idea"?
choices: A hypothesis we want to validate, broken down into PR-sized tasks
questions.explanation: An idea is a hypothesis to validate; it is broken into tasks, each a discrete PR-sized piece of executing it (Engineering Handbook; Studio AI SDLC & MCP).

questions.prompt: Which sequence describes the Studio AI delivery loop?
choices: idea → tasks → pick up task → branch → PR → review → merge (ships)
questions.explanation: Work flows idea → tasks → pick up task → branch → PR → review → merge, and merging ships to production and closes the task (Studio AI SDLC & MCP).

questions.prompt: Which MCP tool do you call to pick up a task and start working on it?
questions.explanation: work_on_next_task picks up a task, moves it to inProgress, and returns the spec plus the task's injected curated context (Studio AI SDLC & MCP).

questions.prompt: When an agent picks up a task, how does it receive the relevant documents?
choices: It has to search the whole knowledge base itself
Studio AI injects the task's curated context (its "neighborhood") into the pickup response
The documents are emailed to the engineer
It clones a separate documentation repository
questions.explanation: At pickup, Studio AI injects the task's curated context — a small neighborhood of the most relevant documents delivered in one shot, instead of forcing the agent to go search (Studio AI SDLC & MCP).

questions.prompt: About how many documents make up a well-curated context "neighborhood" for a task?
questions.explanation: A well-curated neighborhood is roughly 5 documents — the minimum the agent needs and nothing else (Studio AI SDLC & MCP).

questions.prompt: Under the team's trunk-based workflow, what ships a change to production?
choices: Merging a reviewed pull request to main
questions.explanation: You never commit directly to main; all work lands through a reviewed PR, and merging that PR to main is what ships to production (Engineering Handbook).
